title: Routing: enforce residency region pinning + disable cross-region fallback by default
author: Elena Popov
description:
Summary: Integrates Hosted Data Residency “region pinning” policy evaluation into Smart Routing decisions. Requests are constrained to the policy’s allowed_regions and will no longer fail over cross-region by default. Adds structured decision context to routing logs/spans for traceability and downstream error shaping.

Why: We’ve had customer incidents where routing attempted cross-region fallback when a customer expected EU-only processing (see SUP-28441). This PR ensures routing respects residency constraints deterministically, and makes the decision observable (selected region, policy source, and block reason).

Behavior changes: 1) Policy evaluation: Router calls ResidencyPolicyService (cached) at request admission to resolve the effective residency policy (API key > project > org precedence). 2) Region selection: Candidate regions list is intersected with policy.allowed_regions. If the intersection is empty, the request is blocked at routing with a typed error (ResViolated) including a reason code; the gateway PR will map this to the public error contract. 3) Fallback: Cross-region fallback is disabled by default when a residency policy is present. If policy.allow_cross_region_failover=true (explicit) then fallback may occur but only within policy.allowed_regions. 4) Dedicated alignment: Dedicated routes already run in a customer-selected region; for shared routing codepaths we still apply the same allowed_regions intersection to avoid accidental spillover.

Observability: Adds a structured “residency_decision” object to router logs and tracing span attributes (no customer content). Fields include policy_source (org/project/api_key), policy_id (internal UUID), allowed_regions (internal region IDs), primary_region, selected_region, fallback_attempted, fallback_blocked, decision (allow|block), block_reason, and eval_latency_ms.

Safety/rollout: Feature-gated behind routing.residency_enforcement.enabled (default OFF). Dogfood plan is to enable in staging first (INT-9312) and then progressive production rollout by org allowlist.

Testing: Adds unit tests for policy precedence, candidate region intersection, and fallback behavior. Adds a routing integration test harness with synthetic policy responses and verifies that the selected region is stable across retries and that cross-region fallback is blocked.

Notes: This PR intentionally does NOT implement the public HTTP error payload. That is handled in pr-21533 (gateway). This PR focuses on routing correctness + decision tracing.
commits: routing: add residency policy evaluation hook + cache
routing: constrain region candidates by allowed_regions + primary_region bias
routing: disable cross-region fallback when policy present (feature-flagged)
observability: add residency_decision log fields + span attributes
tests: precedence + fallback matrix + deterministic selection
chore: docs for new routing flags (internal)
illustrative_snippet: New span/log fields (example): residency_decision.decision=block residency_decision.block_reason=NO_ALLOWED_REGIONS_MATCH residency_decision.policy_source=api_key residency_decision.allowed_regions=["eu-central-1"] residency_decision.primary_region=eu-central-1 residency_decision.selected_region="" residency_decision.fallback_blocked=true
review_conversation: Mina Haddad (review): Candidate region filtering looks right. Can you confirm we never log raw region hostnames or customer org names? Prefer internal IDs only.
Elena Popov (author): Yep—only internal region IDs; no org/project names. I added a guard to avoid logging external-facing region strings and updated the log field doc.

Ravi Menon (review): The fallback change is a behavior shift—please ensure it is strictly behind the flag and default-off. Also: determinism matters; avoid random selection across equally ranked regions.

Elena Popov (author): Updated. The enforcement path is only active when routing.residency_enforcement.enabled=true AND an effective policy is present. Selection is deterministic: stable sort by (primary_region match, health score, price tier, region_id) and we persist the chosen region in the request context for retries.

Marcus Lin (security): Please add an explicit assertion that policy_id is safe to expose internally but not returned to customers. Also confirm no customer prompt/completions flow into telemetry with these fields.
Elena Popov (author): Added comments + unit test ensuring routing errors don’t include policy_id in message text. Also verified fields are set on spans only; payload data is never attached.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we get a metric for fallback_blocked and block_reason counts? Even if dashboards land elsewhere, emitting counters here will help during rollout.

Elena Popov (author): Added counters in routing telemetry: residency.blocks_total{reason,region} and residency.fallback_blocked_total{from,to}. Dashboard work tracked separately in ENG-4846 but metrics are now emitted.
Jordan Lee (policy): Precedence API key > project > org matches the design. Please ensure “no policy configured” remains a no-op.
Elena Popov (author): Confirmed—when no effective policy, routing behavior is unchanged.
ci_notes: First run failed due to a flaky determinism test (seed not set). Rerun after fixing stable sort + explicit seed passed.
rollout_notes: Flag: routing.residency_enforcement.enabled (default OFF). Allowlist: routing.residency_enforcement.allowlisted_orgs=[...]. When enabled, cross-region fallback is blocked unless policy.allow_cross_region_failover=true AND the fallback target is within allowed_regions.
release_notes: Internal: Smart Routing can now enforce residency region pinning and will block cross-region fallback by default when a residency policy is configured. Adds structured routing telemetry for residency decisions to aid auditability and incident response.
